Healthy-patient comparison & sources
ReferenceBlood-volume estimateCollection / recovery guide
Workbook default60 mL/kg × 0.85 = 51 mL/kg adjusted; healthy/baseline option = 60 mL/kg1% / 24 hr; 10% / 14 days
Indiana University IACUCHealthy adult dog: 85 mL/kg1% / 24 hr; 7.5% / 7 days; 10% / 2–4 weeks
NC3RsDog: 70–110 mL/kg; cat: 47–65 mL/kg; breed/individual variation1% / 24 hr for short-interval sampling; 10% single draw with 3–4 weeks before repeating

Interpretation: the workbook’s 60 mL/kg baseline lies within the cited feline range and below the cited canine range. Its 14-day window is shorter than NC3Rs’ 3–4-week recovery guidance. These healthy-animal research references do not validate a universal sick-patient sampling limit or a blood-donation protocol. NC3Rs describes a 15% lower estimate for obese/older animals; illness requires individual assessment rather than assuming that reduction is sufficient.

For a 20 kg patient: workbook adjusted = 1,020 mL total, 10.2 mL / 24 hr and 102 mL / 14 days; baseline = 1,200 mL, 12 mL / 24 hr and 120 mL / 14 days. Using IU’s canine 85 mL/kg estimate gives 1,700 mL total, 17 mL at 1% and 170 mL at 10% (2–4-week interval).
